references.text: Moses expressed similar frustration to God when he asked why God had sent him to Pharaoh, which led to more suffering for the people.
The Israelites complained to Moses at the Red Sea and asked why he had brought them out of Egypt to die in the wilderness, similar to Joshua's complaint about crossing the Jordan.
The people complained that Moses and Aaron had brought them into the wilderness to die, the same type of complaint that Joshua expresses here.
The Israelites asked why the Lord had brought them to the land of Canaan only to fall by the sword, wishing to return, similar to Joshua's words.
The people complained that they were brought out of Egypt to die in the wilderness, the same pattern of complaint against God's leadership.
Moses addresses God as 'Lord my God' in a manner similar to how Joshua uses 'O Lord, Lord' in his prayer.
The Jordan was crossed as described here, the same crossing of the Jordan that Joshua now regrets in his complaint.
Gideon expressed similar doubt when he asked why all this had happened to them if the Lord was with them.
